title: A petition is approved with an invisible name (zero-width characters only), and a problem made only of zero-width characters passes the 5-character minimum
repro: node tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/hunt2-desk/p1.mjs (files fields.name = '\u200B\u200B\u200B')
root_cause: String.prototype.trim() treats U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF as text, so the length checks count them. The repeat code strips them (repeat.ts:36), but the filing schema does not.
where: src/lib/manu/petitions.ts:178 and :187 (z.string().trim().min(2) / .min(5): trim() does not remove U+200B)

title: The same person writing about the same sewage problem, once in Tamil script and once in Tanglish, is told 'written 1 earlier petition on other problems'
repro: node tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/hunt2-desk/p2.mjs: petition A, CMWSSB ward 70, problem 'கழிவுநீர் தெருவில் ஓடுகிறது, துர்நாற்றம்'; repeat check for B with the same mobile, problem 'kazhivu neer theruvil odudhu, smell romba'
root_cause: There is no transliteration between Tamil script and Tanglish/English, so the words never meet. The headline then says 'other problems' confidently, when it should say 'could not tell'. The same happens against an online complaint (p10.mjs): a Tamil petition 'கோவில் அருகே குப்பை அள்ளப்படவில்லை' against the citizen's 'Garbage not cleared near the temple' from the same mobile gives 'on other problems', with no join offered.
where: src/lib/manu/repeat.ts:33-52 (words() and sameTopic compare spellings only); headline at repeat.ts:116

title: Two different people with the same name (different mobiles, different streets) are counted as one: '1 other person has written about this in the same ward'

title: In a ward and department with more than 200 approved petitions, a person's own earlier petition (same mobile) is cut by LIMIT 200 and 'came before' misses it, though the comment says the person's rows have 'a query of their own'
repro: Code reading (not run: flooding). WHERE p.status = 'filed' AND p.id <> ? AND (p.mobile = ? OR p.name = ? OR (p.ward_number = ? AND p.dept_code = ?)) ORDER BY p.filed_at DESC LIMIT 200
root_cause: The 'query of their own' (comment at :138-139) separates them only from the no-ward department query, not from the ward-and-department rows

title: Only one closing SMS is ever sent per petition. A petition rejected (SMS 'could not be taken up'), then reopened by the Collector and done, never gets the 'done' SMS, so the petitioner's last word is the rejection
repro: Code reading, with the live flow it rests on: node tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/hunt2-desk/p22.mjs (2026-910AKR: reject 201, /track 'Rejected'; reopen 201, /track 'In Progress'). title: A 12-digit Aadhaar written in groups other than 4-4-4 (5-7, 6-6, 2-4-6, single spaced digits) is not masked on the console case (nor at the desk)
repro: same probe file as redteam-gate-02, describe '12-digit shapes maskAadhaar does not take'
root_cause: the AADHAAR regex needs three groups of exactly four digits; less common but real ways of writing the number pass whole

title: Test mode: a team-inbox mail that answers after the 20 s limit is marked 'failed' and mailed again
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer1/sms.probe.test.ts -t "team inbox"
root_cause: withLimit rejects with a plain Error, so a timed-out SMTP send is 'failed', not 'unsure'; the mail keeps going behind the race.

title: A live send that times out before it ever connected (provider or network down, dropped SYNs, slow DNS) is 'unsure' and never retried
repro: Read sms.ts:96-101: `if (err.name === "TimeoutError" || err.name === "AbortError" || AFTER_SENDING.has(...)) throw new MaybeSent(...)`. The fix's own test 'a send that timed out after it went out is unsure' shows a TimeoutError -> 'unsure', sweep sends nothing.
root_cause: Classification by error name only; no signal of whether the request body was written (e.g. undici connect timeout UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT is only seen if the connect timeout is shorter than the abort).

title: A petition that joined another petition's case gets its own case on rebuild when it was uploaded first and both were approved in the same second
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer1/cases.probe.test.ts -t "same second"
root_cause: Petitions are rebuilt ORDER BY filed_at, id; filed_at has one-second resolution and id is the upload order, not the approval order, so the attached petition can come before the case it joined. The online-first change fixed only the online case.

title: An approval that fails after the petition is committed never sends the 'registered' SMS, and the desk then says the SMS service is not set up
repro: npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer1/sms.probe.test.ts -t "fails after the petition is filed"
root_cause: The SMS row is only created by sendPetitionSms at the end of filePetition; the 'already filed' early return (line 204) never sends it, and smsNote maps a missing row to 'off' even when smsMode() is live. A restart between the commit and line 250 has the same effect. Not introduced by the fix, but one of the desk states it now names.
